title.en: The Great Depression and the rise of Fascism and Nazism

text.en: On 24 October 1929 share prices in the United States collapsed. Shareholders rushed to sell, nobody wanted to buy, banks failed, and the shock travelled across the world. Within a few years millions had lost their jobs, and in several countries angry people turned to leaders who promised strength and order.

The First World War left Europe weakened and in debt, and the Treaty of Versailles added political complications and a wave of economic nationalism with tariff barriers.
The first huge Stock Market Crash in the USA came on 24 October 1929; American banks failed and financiers withdrew funds invested abroad.
England left the Gold Standard, many countries followed, and each adopted protectionism and devaluation, so world trade and credit contracted sharply: the Great Depression.
The Depression changed politics: Labour lost in England in 1931 and the Republicans were rejected in the USA for about twenty years.
In Italy, unhappy ex-soldiers, industrialists and the middle classes backed Mussolini's Fascist Party, which stood for authority, strength and discipline and freely used violence.
In October 1922 Mussolini organised the Fascist March on Rome and the King invited him to form a government.
Fascism is radical authoritarian ultra-nationalism with dictatorial power and suppression of opposition; in Germany a similar movement, Nazism under Hitler, grew from the humiliation of Versailles and the Depression.

problem.en: A country is hit by a depression, and people blame the government and an old treaty. Why might they turn to a strong leader?

text.en: Hunger and unemployment make people desperate for quick answers.
Strong leaders promise order, jobs and national pride, as Mussolini and Hitler did.
The cost is the loss of freedom and the suppression of opposition.

prompt.en: Explain how the Great Depression helped dictators rise.

requiredIdeas.en: Fascists and Nazis promised strength and order

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the Depression was only an American event

points.en: Great Depression began with the crash of 24 October 1929.
Countries left the Gold Standard and raised tariffs.
Mussolini came to power after the March on Rome, 1922.
Fascism: ultra-nationalist dictatorship; Nazism in Germany.
